summary.headline: Abbott's market odds climb in Texas as Senate control holds steady
paras: Prediction markets give Democrats about a 68% chance of winning the Senate, down about 1 point since the last update, and about a 91% chance of winning the House, little changed. Democrats lead the RealClearPolling generic ballot average 50.5% to 42.4%, unchanged. Polling averages were steady across the Senate and governor races, with only Minnesota's Senate average picking up a new poll that left Peggy Flanagan's 3-point lead intact.

The biggest move came in the Texas governor's race, where Greg Abbott's market odds rose about 4 to 5 points to roughly 73%, even though polls show him ahead of Gina Hinojosa by just over 2 points. In Alaska's governor's race, Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins slipped about 4 points but remains a strong favorite at about 85%, and in Virginia's 1st District Democrat Shannon Taylor gained about 3 points to about 64%. Texas and Maine remain the tightest high-profile Senate contests in polling, while Ohio's governor's race continues to feel the fallout from Vivek Ramaswamy's ad featuring Amy Acton's estranged mother, with Acton at about 82% in the markets.

measures.title: Housing and veterans bond
measures.yes: Borrow $11.25 billion for affordable housing, veterans' home loans and youth housing.

measures.title: Bigger rainy-day fund
measures.yes: Raise the cap on the state's reserve fund from 10% to 20% of general fund revenue.

measures.title: Extend high-earner income taxes
measures.yes: Renew the extra income taxes on high earners first passed in 2012, which fund schools and early childhood programs.

measures.title: Public campaign financing
measures.yes: Let state and local governments give candidates public funds if they accept spending limits.

measures.title: No replacement vote in recalls
measures.yes: End the replacement-candidate election when a state official is recalled; the vacancy would be filled under state law instead.

measures.title: Homebuyer second-mortgage program
measures.yes: Create a second-mortgage program for qualifying homebuyers, funded by $25 billion in bonds.

measures.title: Immunology research bonds
measures.yes: Borrow $8.4 billion to fund immunology and immunotherapy research.

measures.title: Voter ID and citizenship checks
measures.yes: Require government-issued ID to vote and have officials verify citizenship using government data.

measures.title: One-time billionaire wealth tax
measures.yes: Impose a one-time 5% tax on fortunes over $1 billion to fund health care, food aid and schools.

measures.title: Performance rules for new taxes
measures.yes: Require agencies funded by new special taxes to cut their lowest-performing programs and reinvest the savings.

measures.title: Ban new taxes on savings and wealth
measures.yes: Block new taxes, enacted after Jan. 1, 2026, on retirement accounts, personal assets and savings.

measures.title: Two-thirds vote for local special taxes
measures.yes: Require a two-thirds public vote to pass, extend or raise local special taxes placed on the ballot by initiative.

measures.title: Spending rule for community clinics
measures.yes: Require federally qualified health centers to spend at least 90% of revenue on their mission.

measures.title: Faster permits for essential projects
measures.yes: Set deadlines for agencies to review housing, water, transit, energy and public-safety projects.

measures.title: Immigration notice to federal officials
measures.yes: Require police to notify Homeland Security when someone charged with a violent crime, or with a prior felony, has an immigration status that can't be confirmed.

measures.title: Right to buy natural gas
measures.yes: Guarantee consumers a constitutional right to buy natural gas for cooking and heating.

measures.title: Right to hunt and fish
measures.yes: Add a right to hunt and fish to the state constitution, still subject to state regulation.

measures.title: ID on mail ballots
measures.yes: Require mail voters to include their signature and a form of ID with their ballot.

measures.title: Plain-language ballot questions
measures.yes: Require ballot questions to be written at or below an eighth-grade reading level.

measures.title: Court approval of 2028 congressional map
measures.yes: Require the 2028 congressional map to be approved by a nonpolitical commission and the state supreme court.

measures.title: Graduated income tax
measures.yes: Replace the flat income tax with a graduated one, with higher rates on higher incomes.

measures.title: Tougher fentanyl penalties
measures.yes: Raise penalties for fentanyl felonies and require treatment for some drug offenses.

measures.title: Life sentence for child sex trafficking
measures.yes: Require life without parole for trafficking a child for sexual servitude.

measures.title: School sports separated by sex
measures.yes: Require K-12 and college teams to be separated by biological sex unless co-ed.

measures.title: Ban gender surgery for minors
measures.yes: Prohibit gender-related surgeries for patients under 18.

measures.title: Cap income tax rates at 4.4%
measures.yes: Cap individual and corporate income tax rates at 4.4%.

measures.title: Keep sporting-goods sales tax for conservation
measures.yes: Let the state keep sales tax from sporting goods for water, land, wildfire prevention and recreation.

measures.title: Raise TABOR cap for schools
measures.yes: Raise the state's TABOR revenue cap and spend the surplus on K-12 education.

measures.title: Larger budget reserve
measures.yes: Let the state keep up to 25% of general revenue in its budget stabilization fund, up from 10%.

measures.title: Farm equipment tax exemption
measures.yes: Exempt farm equipment and other agricultural property from property taxes.

measures.title: Property tax relief
measures.yes: Raise the homestead exemption, tighten the cap on assessment increases for other property, and limit how local governments spend property tax revenue.

measures.title: Open the Legislature's and governor's records
measures.yes: Make records held by the Legislature and the governor's office subject to the public records law.

measures.title: Union rights for public defenders
measures.yes: Allow public defenders and other public counsel staff to bargain collectively.

measures.title: Single all-party primary
measures.yes: Replace party primaries with one primary for all candidates; the top two advance.

measures.title: Same-day voter registration
measures.yes: Let people register and vote on the same day.

measures.title: Change the state revenue limit
measures.yes: Change the cap on how much revenue the state can collect each year.

measures.title: Nature conservation fund
measures.yes: Create a dedicated state fund for nature conservation.

measures.title: Single-family homes on smaller lots
measures.yes: Require towns to allow single-family homes on residential lots of at least 5,000 square feet.

measures.title: Repeal recreational marijuana sales
measures.yes: Repeal the laws allowing recreational marijuana sales and home growing.

measures.title: Keep the 2024 gun law
measures.yes: A yes vote keeps the 2024 law that tightened rules on ghost guns and assault weapons; a no vote repeals it.

measures.title: Parents' rights in schools
measures.yes: Re-enact the 2024 parental rights law on reviewing school materials and opting children out of sex education.

measures.title: Girls' sports limited by biological sex
measures.yes: Bar students born male from competing in girls' school and nonprofit sports.

measures.title: Repeal the millionaire income tax
measures.yes: Repeal the tax on household income over $1 million and ban state and local income taxes.

TX.note: Texas usually votes on constitutional amendments in odd-numbered years.

candidates.note: Positions summarized from news coverage, voter guides and campaign statements; each links to its source.

cands.name: James Talarico
cands.bio: Democratic state lawmaker who made affordability, public schools and reproductive rights the center of his campaign.

Abortion.t: Supports putting Roe v. Wade into federal law and calls Texas's ban dangerous.

Border and immigration.t: Backs strict border screening plus a path to citizenship for immigrant workers and families; voted against the state's SB 4 enforcement law.

Cost of living.t: Ties high costs to corruption and wants to repeal Texas's sales-tax break for data centers.

Energy and climate.t: Calls climate change a top priority and backs geothermal and hydrogen jobs.

pitch.t: Casts Paxton as part of a corrupt establishment that serves itself, not Texans.

cands.name: Ken Paxton
cands.bio: Three-term Republican attorney general who beat Sen. John Cornyn in the primary; impeached by the Texas House in 2023 and acquitted by the state Senate.

Abortion.t: Supports Texas's near-total ban; sued out-of-state providers who mail abortion pills to Texans.

Border and immigration.t: Sued the Biden administration over border policy, backed SB 4 and pledges to support Trump's border agenda; endorsed by the National Border Patrol Council.

Cost of living.t: No detailed economic plan found in campaign coverage; he has focused on cultural issues and his record as attorney general.

Energy and climate.t: Opposes climate-focused policy; sued asset managers to protect the coal industry.

pitch.t: Says Talarico's past criticism of capitalism and fossil fuels shows he is too liberal for Texas.

cands.name: Sherrod Brown
cands.bio: Democrat who represented Ohio in the Senate for 18 years before losing in 2024; running for the seat Vance left.

Abortion.t: Supports legal abortion and backed Ohio's 2023 constitutional amendment protecting it.

Health care.t: Attacks Husted's votes for large Medicaid and SNAP cuts in the 2025 tax and spending law.

Iran war.t: Says Husted's votes on the Iran war have raised costs for truckers, farmers and consumers.

Cost of living.t: Runs on a pro-worker record and says Husted sides with corporations over Ohioans.

pitch.t: "Jon Husted stands with corporations, not with Ohioans."

cands.name: Jon Husted
cands.bio: Republican former lieutenant governor, appointed to the Senate when JD Vance became vice president.

Abortion.t: Supported overturning Roe and opposed Ohio's abortion-rights amendment; sponsored a bill barring federal funds for abortion.

Health care.t: Voted for the 2025 tax and spending law, including its Medicaid and SNAP changes.

Iran war.t: Brown attacks his votes on the Iran war; we found no Husted statement on the war in campaign coverage.

Cost of living.t: Backs cutting "bureaucratic red tape" for Ohio businesses and has pushed a bill on data center utility costs.

pitch.t: Says Ohio voters already rejected Brown's decades-long Washington record in 2024.

cands.name: Troy Jackson
cands.bio: Democrat and former logger from northern Maine, nominated at a July convention after Graham Platner withdrew.

Abortion.t: Supports abortion rights and attacks Collins's 2018 vote for Justice Kavanaugh; he opposed abortion early in his career and has since reversed.

Iran war.t: Says Collins gave Trump a "blank check" for the Iran war, raising costs at home.

Cost of living.t: Focuses on health care, prescription drugs, child care and nursing-home closures; blames Republican policies for higher prices.

Independence from Trump.t: Says Trump gets Collins's vote whenever he really needs it.

pitch.t: A working-class candidate who says Collins enables Trump on the votes that matter.

cands.name: Susan Collins
cands.bio: Republican seeking a sixth term; chairs the Senate Appropriations Committee.

Abortion.t: Supports federal abortion protections and says she wrote a bill to codify Roe; stands by her Kavanaugh vote.

Iran war.t: Was one of the first Republicans to back a resolution to rein in the Iran war, in April.

Cost of living.t: Blames Jackson's legislative leadership for Maine's high electricity rates and touts federal money she secured as Appropriations chair.

Independence from Trump.t: Says she has voted against her party more than any other senator and opposed the Canada tariffs.

pitch.t: An independent voice who delivers for Maine from a senior seat.

cands.name: Abdul El-Sayed
cands.bio: Progressive Democrat and public health official backed by Sen. Bernie Sanders; narrowly won the August primary.

Health care.t: Backs Medicare for All, with no premiums, copays or deductibles.

Abortion.t: Would codify Roe v. Wade and sponsor the Women's Health Protection Act.

Gas prices and tariffs.t: Supports a temporary gas-tax pause and is open to price controls on domestic oil; favors targeted tariffs backed by the UAW over broad ones.

Iran and Israel.t: Opposed the Iran war and said he would not send defensive weapons to Israel.

pitch.t: Ties Rogers to Trump, corporate interests and the Iran war.

cands.name: Mike Rogers
cands.bio: Republican former congressman and House Intelligence Committee chair, endorsed by Trump; narrowly lost Michigan's 2024 Senate race.

Health care.t: Opposes Medicare for All, saying it would end private coverage and require big tax increases.

Abortion.t: Calls himself pro-life but opposes a national ban; says states should decide.

Gas prices and tariffs.t: Rejects price controls; backs gas-tax relief, diesel rebates and a pause on diesel exports. Says some tariffs helped Michigan but wants a negotiated deal.

Iran and Israel.t: Supported the initial strikes on Iran, later called for ending them quickly; backs defensive weapons for Israel.

pitch.t: Says El-Sayed's agenda is too costly and too far left for Michigan.

cands.name: Josh Turek
cands.bio: Democrat from Council Bluffs running for the open seat left by retiring Sen. Joni Ernst.

Farm policy and tariffs.t: Wants the administration's tariffs ended and supports federal right-to-repair for farm equipment.

Health care.t: Would reverse the 2025 law's Medicaid and SNAP cuts, which he says hurt rural hospitals.

Taxes.t: Backs keeping the tax breaks on tips, overtime and Social Security; also wants a higher minimum wage and a federal ban on food price gouging.

Iran war.t: Blames the Iran war for record diesel prices and has pressed Hinson on war-powers votes.

pitch.t: Says Washington changed Hinson and focuses on her family's growing wealth.

cands.name: Ashley Hinson
cands.bio: Republican congresswoman from eastern Iowa and former TV news anchor, endorsed by Trump.

Farm policy and tariffs.t: Says she is the candidate who will fight for farmers; criticizes Turek's record on farm votes.

Health care.t: Defends the 2025 law as tax relief and says its Medicaid changes target fraud.

Taxes.t: Runs on "no tax on tips, no tax on overtime" and lower taxes on Social Security.

Iran war.t: Has voted against resolutions to end the war; broke with Trump on a Russian diesel deal.

pitch.t: A bipartisan problem-solver focused on lower costs, veterans and farmers.

cands.name: Pete Ricketts
cands.bio: Republican former two-term governor, appointed to the Senate in 2023 and elected to finish the term in 2024.

Tariffs and costs.t: Defends targeted tariffs to level the field for U.S. products; blames inflation on Biden-era policies.

Iran war.t: Calls Iran a direct threat and backs continued economic and diplomatic pressure.

Health care.t: Says the 2025 law's Medicaid changes protect eligible patients, cut fraud and steady rural hospitals.

Abortion.t: Supports a 12-week limit and would write a 13-week ban into the state constitution.

pitch.t: Calls Osborn "Democrat Dan" and says refusing to caucus with a party is unworkable.

cands.name: Dan Osborn
cands.bio: Independent who led a 2021 Kellogg's strike; lost to Sen. Deb Fischer by about 7 points in 2024.

Tariffs and costs.t: Says targeted tariffs can work but broad ones raise costs; wants Congress to reclaim tariff power.

Iran war.t: Agrees Iran must not get a nuclear weapon but says Congress should authorize military action; ties the war to fuel and fertilizer costs.

Health care.t: Warns the Medicaid changes will hurt rural hospitals and patients.

Abortion.t: Personally pro-life but says government should not make health decisions for people.

pitch.t: A working-class independent who won't caucus with either party.

cands.name: Roger Marshall
cands.bio: Republican and former OB-GYN seeking a second term; endorsed by Trump.

Abortion.t: Opposes abortion.

Tariffs and farms.t: Says tariffs bring short-term pain but long-term gain for farmers.

Health care.t: Pushes price transparency and going after fraud in the Affordable Care Act; backed repealing the ACA in 2017.

Government reform.t: Joined Hamilton in opposing Trump's threat to block sales by Bombardier, a major Wichita employer.

pitch.t: Calls Hamilton "the ultimate snake oil salesman" hiding liberal views.

cands.name: Adam Hamilton
cands.bio: Democrat and longtime pastor in suburban Kansas City; endorsed by two former Republican governors.

Abortion.t: Supports abortion rights.

Tariffs and farms.t: Opposes the tariffs and says they and the Iran war raised family costs.

Health care.t: Criticizes cuts to Medicaid and food aid but backs cutting Medicaid "waste, fraud and abuse".

Government reform.t: Wants a ban on stock trading by lawmakers, term or age limits, and data centers paying for their own power.

pitch.t: A moderate who rejects "both extremes" and calls Marshall a Washington "yes man".

cands.name: Mary Peltola
cands.bio: Democrat who held Alaska's House seat from 2022 to 2025; led the August all-party primary.

Energy.t: Points to the Willow oil project's approval as a delegation win she helped deliver.

Iran war.t: Says the war is driving up Alaskans' energy bills with no end in sight.

Health care.t: Blames Congress for Medicaid cuts and higher costs in a state that already pays more for care.

Fisheries.t: Accuses Sullivan of siding with industry donors on bycatch.

pitch.t: Says Alaskans are tired of dishonesty and need someone who fights for fish, not donations.

cands.name: Dan Sullivan
cands.bio: Republican and Marine Corps Reserve officer seeking a third term.

Energy.t: Says producing more Alaska energy is the way to cut costs; credits regulatory rollbacks under Trump.

Iran war.t: Wants the war to end soon, once the Strait of Hormuz reopens and Iran is kept from a nuclear weapon.

Health care.t: Voted for the 2025 law that cut Medicaid, but broke with Republicans to back extending ACA subsidies.

Fisheries.t: Has a bycatch bill he says could soon get a committee vote.

pitch.t: Says Peltola backed the Biden administration's limits on Alaska resource development.

cands.name: Chris Pappas
cands.bio: Democrat who has represented New Hampshire's 1st District since 2019; running for the seat Sen. Jeanne Shaheen is leaving.

Cost of living.t: Blames tariffs, health subsidy cuts and high gas and grocery prices.

Health care.t: Would restore the expanded ACA premium credits and hold insurers and drugmakers accountable.

Iran war.t: Says the war hurts national security and raises gas prices.

Social Security.t: Pledges to protect Social Security and Medicare and says Sununu once pushed privatization.

pitch.t: Frames the race as a choice about Trump's leadership.

cands.name: John E. Sununu
cands.bio: Republican who served in the Senate from 2003 to 2009; endorsed by Trump.

Cost of living.t: Makes affordability his main theme and accuses Pappas of backing runaway spending and tax increases.

Health care.t: Backed the 2025 tax and spending law; proposes making members of Congress pay the full cost of their own health care.

Iran war.t: Says he disagreed with the decision to attack Iran and opposes a proposed $300 billion reconstruction fund.

Social Security.t: Backed private accounts during his earlier Senate term, according to Pappas; also supports congressional term limits.

pitch.t: Says eight years of Pappas in Congress "hasn't delivered" for New Hampshire.

cands.name: Peggy Flanagan
cands.bio: Democrat and two-term lieutenant governor under Tim Walz; would be Minnesota's first Native American senator.

Iran and Israel.t: Would vote against more Iran war funding and offensive weapons for Israel.

Immigration.t: Supports strong borders but wants to "tear ICE apart" and create a path to citizenship.

Health care.t: Backs Medicare for All.

Fraud.t: Says more should have been done on state program fraud but that she did not lead that work.

pitch.t: Says Tafoya would be a rubber stamp for Trump.

cands.name: Michele Tafoya
cands.bio: Republican and former NBC sideline reporter, endorsed by Trump; calls herself a "pro-choice Republican".

Iran and Israel.t: Wants the Iran war to end quickly and "strategically"; says "I stand with Israel".

Immigration.t: Opposes abolishing ICE and says immigrants convicted of fraud should be deported.

Health care.t: Opposes Medicare for All and says the ACA has not made care cheaper.

Fraud.t: Makes the state's fraud scandals her main attack and ties Flanagan to the Walz administration.

pitch.t: Says Flanagan shares the blame for Minnesota's fraud scandals.

cands.name: Darline Graham Nordone
cands.bio: Republican appointed after the death of her brother, Sen. Lindsey Graham; endorsed by Trump. First run for office.

Health care.t: Opposes "government run health care for all," saying it would add to the debt; supports Medicare for seniors and vulnerable people.

Taxes and spending.t: Says her priority is economic relief from grocery and gas prices.

National security.t: Said in an August debate that national security is "not my thing"; avoided a repeat in October.

Social issues.t: Opposes abortion, backs keeping men out of women's sports and calls the SAVE Act on voter citizenship her top priority.

pitch.t: Says Andrews would join the "socialist Democrats" in Washington.

cands.name: Annie Andrews
cands.bio: Democrat and Charleston children's doctor; ran for the House in 2022.

Health care.t: Backs an optional government health plan, Medicaid expansion and restoring ACA subsidies; says she does not support Medicare for All.

Taxes and spending.t: Wants to cut the deficit, lower taxes for working families and trim congressional perks.

National security.t: Says Graham is not ready to serve "during wartime".

Social issues.t: Has responded with an ad to anti-transgender attacks echoed by Trump.

pitch.t: Calls Graham "unserious and unqualified" and the White House's ambassador to South Carolina.

cands.name: Rick Jackson
cands.bio: Republican billionaire who founded a health care staffing company; beat Trump-backed Lt. Gov. Burt Jones in the June runoff.

Health care.t: Wants a partial Medicaid expansion funded by a federal block grant, and vows to stop insurers' claim denials.

Taxes and costs.t: Promises to cut the state income tax in his first term "or I won't run again".

Education.t: Would cut paperwork for teachers and introduce technical careers earlier.

Data centers.t: Would approve them only with local consent, strict standards and discounted bills for neighbors.

pitch.t: Attacks Bottoms's record as Atlanta mayor.

cands.name: Keisha Lance Bottoms
cands.bio: Democrat who led Atlanta from 2018 to 2022 and later served in the Biden White House.

Health care.t: Makes full Medicaid expansion a top priority to save rural hospitals.

Taxes and costs.t: Would suspend the grocery tax and raise the state minimum wage.

Education.t: Would raise starting teacher pay to $60,000 and make technical college free.

Data centers.t: Wants a pause on new data centers while the state studies their effects.

pitch.t: Ties Jackson to Trump's agenda, including cuts at Veterans Affairs.

cands.name: Aaron Ford
cands.bio: Democrat in his second term as attorney general; would be Nevada's first Black governor.

Cost of living.t: Wants universal free school meals, a $35 insulin cap, expanded paid family leave and an end to NV Energy's demand charge.

Abortion.t: Supports abortion rights and backed the 2024 ballot measure protecting them.

Data centers and energy.t: Would require data centers to supply their own power and pause tax breaks for them; backs residential solar.

pitch.t: Calls it the "Lombardo-Trump economy" and runs on lowering costs.

cands.name: Joe Lombardo
cands.bio: Republican former Clark County sheriff seeking a second term.

Cost of living.t: Vetoed the bills behind Ford's agenda, saying the vetoes protected Nevada; credits his tenure with falling inflation and job growth.

Abortion.t: Calls himself "pro-life with exceptions" and says the issue belongs to Nevada voters; opposed the 2024 abortion-rights measure.

Data centers and energy.t: Says current rules already shield ratepayers; pulled Nevada out of the U.S. Climate Alliance to focus on energy costs.

pitch.t: Says Ford's agenda would cost $18 billion and questions his record on crime.

cands.name: Amy Acton
cands.bio: Democrat and physician who led Ohio's health department early in the COVID-19 pandemic.

Taxes.t: Wants middle-class tax cuts and a child tax credit.

Health care.t: Would use public money to erase medical debt for qualifying Ohioans and use state buying power to cut drug prices.

Abortion.t: Supports legal abortion access.

Data centers and energy.t: Wants more transparency and regulation for data centers and fewer incentives.

pitch.t: Says Ramaswamy is out of touch with middle-class Ohioans.

cands.name: Vivek Ramaswamy
cands.bio: Republican biotech entrepreneur and 2024 presidential candidate, endorsed by Trump.

Taxes.t: Pledged to end the state income tax and promises the largest property tax rollback in Ohio history.

Health care.t: Supports work requirements for Medicaid and other benefits.

Abortion.t: Calls himself pro-life, says abortion is a state matter and has backed a ban around six weeks.

Data centers and energy.t: Focuses on expanding energy supply and cutting red tape to lower costs.

pitch.t: Attacks Acton's COVID-era record, including postponing the 2020 primary.

cands.name: Greg Abbott
cands.bio: Republican seeking a record fourth term.

Schools and vouchers.t: Made private school vouchers his top legislative priority and calls the program a signature achievement.

Property taxes.t: Proposes letting voters abolish school property taxes, requiring two-thirds voter approval for tax hikes and cutting the appraisal cap to 3%.

Border.t: Runs on the state's border crackdown, Operation Lone Star, and stricter bail.

Data centers.t: Reversed past support and now calls for blocking new data centers in rural Texas.

pitch.t: "Don't let Gina deceive you, Texas." Pledges to keep Texas a "bastion of common sense".

cands.name: Gina Hinojosa
cands.bio: Democrat from Austin and former school board president.

Schools and vouchers.t: Opposes the voucher program and wants more state money for public schools.

Property taxes.t: Says property taxes are too high.

Border.t: Criticizes the $11 billion spent on Operation Lone Star and wants federal reimbursement.

Data centers.t: Vows a moratorium on new data centers.

pitch.t: Says billionaires and corporations are driving up prices and closing neighborhood schools.

cands.name: Phil Scott
cands.bio: Moderate Republican seeking a sixth two-year term; a social liberal and fiscal conservative who has often broken with Trump.

Taxes and costs.t: Says reaching for new taxes is the wrong answer; holds the state record for vetoes.

Health care.t: Says the state should fix the systems already in place rather than add new taxes and programs.

Schools.t: Backs school consolidation to cut education costs.

Housing.t: Blames the Democratic Legislature for blocking his growth and housing proposals.

pitch.t: A pragmatic, incremental governor willing to compromise when it makes sense for Vermonters.

cands.name: Amanda Janoo
cands.bio: Democrat and political newcomer from Strafford who worked in economic development for the United Nations.

Taxes and costs.t: Leans on higher taxes for wealthy Vermonters and backing local production and jobs.

Health care.t: Proposes the first state-funded universal primary care system.

Schools.t: Opposes closing schools that hold communities together.

Housing.t: Would invest in permanently affordable housing.

pitch.t: Says problems have worsened under Scott and the system rewards money over work.

cands.name: Tina Kotek
cands.bio: Democrat and former Oregon House speaker; beat Drazan by about 4 points in 2022.

Taxes and costs.t: Did not commit to tax changes; says Drazan voted against a low-income tax break.

Housing and homelessness.t: Points to her executive orders on homelessness and housing production.

Data centers.t: Backs a moratorium on new data centers and signed the POWER Act on large power users' rates.

Elections.t: Would fight changes to Oregon's vote-by-mail system.

pitch.t: Says Drazan would side with Trump instead of Oregon.

cands.name: Christine Drazan
cands.bio: Republican and former Oregon House minority leader, in a rematch of 2022.

Taxes and costs.t: Promises to veto new taxes and fees and cut rules that raise living costs.

Housing and homelessness.t: Calls Kotek's approach "an abysmal failure"; wants faster permits, more land and measurable results.

Data centers.t: Also backs a moratorium, though she voted against the POWER Act.

Elections.t: Wants polling places back and backed a bill to make in-person voting with ID the norm.

pitch.t: Says Kotek answers every problem with a new tax.

cands.name: Byron Donalds
cands.bio: Republican congressman from southwest Florida, endorsed by Trump.

Abortion.t: Has not proposed changes to Florida's current abortion law in coverage we found.

Insurance costs.t: Promises to cut insurance costs 20% in his first year.

Education.t: Would keep and expand school choice.

Environment.t: Lists preserving the environment and infrastructure among his seven priorities, alongside enacting Trump's agenda.

pitch.t: Says Jolly has made a "complete 180" on abortion and immigration since leaving the GOP.

cands.name: David Jolly
cands.bio: Former Republican congressman from Pinellas County who left the GOP in 2018 and now runs as a Democrat.

Abortion.t: Supports restoring Roe-style protections and would veto new restrictions.

Insurance costs.t: Makes the insurance and affordability crisis a top priority.

Education.t: Calls public education a crisis and wants politicians out of classrooms.

Environment.t: Opposes Gulf oil drilling and backs a moratorium on large data centers.

pitch.t: Says a Donalds governorship would be more of the same, carrying out the Trump agenda.

cands.name: David Crowley
cands.bio: Democrat who won an upset primary for the open seat Gov. Tony Evers is leaving.

Data centers.t: Now says he would sign a repeal of data center tax breaks, after earlier calling for a review instead.

Taxes and costs.t: Names cost of living and workforce investment as top priorities.

Schools.t: Wants to fully fund public schools.

Immigration.t: Said at the Oct. 21 debate that local law enforcement should not have contracts with ICE.

pitch.t: Wants to regulate AI and social media and take on rising costs.

cands.name: Tom Tiffany
cands.bio: Republican congressman from northern Wisconsin and House Freedom Caucus member, endorsed by Trump.

Data centers.t: Would end the sales-tax exemption for data centers, let communities weigh in and ban nondisclosure deals.

Taxes and costs.t: Pledges to freeze property taxes and lower energy costs.

Schools.t: Says schools are in "free fall" after years of Democratic control.

Immigration.t: Wants local and state police to work closely with ICE.

pitch.t: Calls his opponent "Data Center David" and says he would give data centers a blank check.

cands.name: Katie Hobbs
cands.bio: Democrat and former secretary of state; running with former Republican Mesa Mayor John Giles.

Abortion.t: Signed the repeal of Arizona's 1864 abortion ban.

Cost of living.t: Blames Trump's tariffs for higher costs; her office has erased over $1 billion in medical debt.

Energy.t: Has pushed solar development on state land.

Elections.t: Declined to debate Biggs, saying she'd rather meet voters directly.

pitch.t: A bipartisan ticket focused on housing, water and the border.

cands.name: Andy Biggs
cands.bio: Republican and former House Freedom Caucus chair, backed by Trump and Turning Point Action.

Abortion.t: Sponsored federal legislation to ban abortion nationwide.

Cost of living.t: Runs on lower taxes and border security.

Energy.t: Voted against the 2022 law's $369 billion in clean energy spending.

Elections.t: Voted against certifying Arizona's 2020 electoral votes.

pitch.t: Says Hobbs is hiding from voters by skipping debates.

cands.name: Rob Sand
cands.bio: Democrat and the only Democrat holding statewide office in Iowa.

Abortion.t: Says the six-week ban "goes too far" and would veto further limits on abortion, contraception or IVF.

Schools.t: Proposes working with the Republican Legislature on "common-sense" issues; no detailed school plan found.

Data centers and farms.t: Has talked about cutting nitrate levels in water and helping farmers.

Cost of living.t: Would cap utility fees, raise the minimum wage, end Medicaid privatization and import cheaper drugs from Canada.

pitch.t: "A new path" after a decade of all-Republican control.

cands.name: Zach Lahn
cands.bio: Republican who narrowly beat Trump-backed Rep. Randy Feenstra in the primary; Trump later endorsed him.

Abortion.t: "Unapologetically pro-life"; supports the six-week ban and would likely back further limits.

Schools.t: Supports vouchers and school competition; says innovation, not money, is the answer.

Data centers and farms.t: Calls for a moratorium on new data centers and disclosure of who owns Iowa farmland.

Cost of living.t: Focuses on lowering taxes and breaking up consolidation in agriculture.

pitch.t: Says Sand is a "liberal billionaire" whose nonpartisan image is a front.

cands.name: Ty Masterson
cands.bio: Republican who has led the state Senate since 2021, endorsed by Trump.

Taxes.t: Calls property taxes a "crisis" and wants a Colorado-style cap on local tax growth.

Abortion.t: Says most people want fewer abortions, no late-term procedures and no taxpayer funding.

Data centers.t: Still backs the data center tax incentives in SB 98.

Health care.t: Opposes Medicaid expansion, calling it a failure at saving rural hospitals.

pitch.t: The most pro-business, pro-ag, pro-oil and gas governor Kansas has had.

cands.name: Cindy Holscher
cands.bio: Democrat from Johnson County running to succeed term-limited Gov. Laura Kelly.

Taxes.t: Blames unfunded special-ed mandates and corporate incentive deals for rising property taxes.

Abortion.t: Supports abortion rights.

Data centers.t: Now backs a statewide moratorium and more guardrails.

Health care.t: Calls Medicaid expansion the biggest thing the state could do for rural hospitals.

pitch.t: Says Masterson is dodging debates and favors billionaire giveaways.

cands.name: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins
cands.bio: Democrat from Sitka and the only Democrat on the ranked-choice ballot.

State budget and dividend.t: Wants a sustainably balanced budget, even if that means a smaller dividend than the old formula.

Education.t: Says his first bill would forward-fund K-12 schools.

Regulation.t: No detailed position found in debate coverage.

Working across parties.t: Says compromise matters and Wilson would extend the gridlock of the Dunleavy years.

pitch.t: "If you like the last eight years, you can get four more."

cands.name: Bernadette Wilson
cands.bio: Republican and former radio host; the top Republican in the August primary.

State budget and dividend.t: Backs paying the full statutory dividend, about $3,800 this year, and an audit to find savings.

Education.t: No detailed education plan found in debate coverage.

Regulation.t: Says her first bill would roll back regulations and end automatic voter registration through the dividend application.

Working across parties.t: Mocks "singing Kumbaya" and asks what bipartisan coalitions have delivered.

pitch.t: Has urged the other two Republicans to drop out so the GOP can consolidate.

cands.name: Sean McCann
cands.bio: Democrat from Kalamazoo, endorsed by Gov. Gretchen Whitmer.

Cost of living.t: Promises tax relief for families and seniors and focuses on gas, housing and child care costs.

Health care.t: Pledges to protect Social Security and health care and supports abortion rights.

pitch.t: Says Republican self-interest is undermining the American Dream.

cands.name: Bill Huizenga
cands.bio: Republican seeking a ninth term; won his last two races by about 12 points.

Cost of living.t: Voted for the 2025 tax and spending law, including its tax cuts.

Health care.t: Backed the law's Medicaid changes, which Democrats say will reduce enrollment.

cands.name: Pia Dandiya
cands.bio: Democrat raised in Palm Beach County; former Harlem high school principal and White House Fellow.

Health care.t: Defends the Affordable Care Act and says Askar would gut health care.

Cost of living.t: Says Askar's health care stance would raise costs for struggling families.

pitch.t: Would be Florida's first South Asian American member of Congress.

cands.name: Casey Askar
cands.bio: Republican and Marine veteran, endorsed by Trump, running for a redrawn open seat.

Health care.t: Wants to end the Affordable Care Act "once and for all".

Cost of living.t: Promises a permanent cut to the federal gas tax.

pitch.t: A businessman and veteran aligned with Trump's agenda.

cands.name: Shannon Taylor
cands.bio: Democrat and longtime commonwealth's attorney; narrowly lost the 2025 primary for state attorney general.

Health care.t: Would restore Medicaid funding and ACA subsidies and get private equity out of health care.

Ethics.t: Wants to ban stock trading by members of Congress.

Border.t: No detailed position found in campaign coverage.

pitch.t: Says tax breaks on tips mean little if health care costs double.

cands.name: Rob Wittman
cands.bio: Republican seeking an eighth full term.

Health care.t: Voted for the 2025 tax and spending law, including its Medicaid changes.

Ethics.t: Pledges to guard against wasteful federal spending.

Border.t: Supports more border security, including a wall on the Mexico border.

cands.name: Cait Conley
cands.bio: Democrat and former National Security Council staffer; describes herself as a moderate.

Immigration.t: Wants to rein in ICE and calls Trump's agenda unlawful and authoritarian.

Cost of living.t: Focuses on affordability, reining in utility monopolies and undoing parts of the 2025 tax and spending law.

Congress and reform.t: Backs 12-year term limits for members of Congress.

pitch.t: Ties Lawler to Trump and MAGA.

cands.name: Mike Lawler
cands.bio: Republican seeking a third term.

Immigration.t: Supports ICE but opposes ending temporary protected status for Haitians.

Cost of living.t: No detailed plan found in debate coverage.

Congress and reform.t: Voted against an Iran war-powers resolution.

pitch.t: Ties Conley to New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and socialism.

cands.name: Mitchell Berman
cands.bio: Democrat raised on a Wisconsin dairy farm; endorsed by the United Auto Workers.

Health care.t: Wants to fix a "broken" health system and criticizes the 2025 law's Medicaid and food aid cuts.

Cost of living.t: Focuses on health care, child care and grocery costs and ending corruption in Washington.

pitch.t: Says Steil had four terms to deliver and didn't.

cands.name: Bryan Steil
cands.bio: Republican from Janesville in Paul Ryan's former seat.

Health care.t: Voted for the 2025 tax and spending law, including its Medicaid changes.

Cost of living.t: No detailed plan found in campaign coverage.

cands.name: Matt Dunlap
cands.bio: Democrat and former Maine secretary of state, running for the open seat Rep. Jared Golden is leaving.

Health care.t: Backed Medicare for All in the primary; says restoring ACA subsidies is the immediate step.

Iran war and energy.t: Ties the war to heating oil above $6 a gallon in the most oil-dependent state.

pitch.t: Says LePage would get rid of Medicaid and won't face voters at town halls.

cands.name: Paul LePage
cands.bio: Republican who served two terms as governor, 2011 to 2019.

Health care.t: Cut state health programs and vetoed MaineCare expansion as governor; focuses on fraud in health programs.

Iran war and energy.t: Says he disagrees with Trump on tariffs, immigration and the Iran war but opposes congressional limits on him.

pitch.t: Says he has a record of cutting costs and taxes and protecting Social Security.

cands.name: William Lawrence
cands.bio: Democrat endorsed by Sen. Bernie Sanders; won the August primary over more moderate rivals.

Foreign policy.t: Wants to end the Iran war and U.S. support for Israel's actions in Gaza.

Data centers.t: Backs a federal moratorium on new AI data centers.

Health care.t: Supports Medicare for All.

pitch.t: Says Barrett cut health care and gave tax breaks to data center developers.

cands.name: Tom Barrett
cands.bio: Republican and 21-year Army helicopter pilot; won the seat by about 4 points in 2024.

Foreign policy.t: Discussed Iran and public safety with Speaker Mike Johnson on the trail.

Data centers.t: No detailed position found in campaign coverage.

Health care.t: No detailed plan found; Lawrence attacks his health care votes.

pitch.t: Says being a socialist should disqualify Lawrence in his district.

cands.name: Bob Harvie
cands.bio: Democrat backed by Gov. Josh Shapiro and endorsed by the Philadelphia Inquirer.

Health care.t: Wants to reverse the effects of Trump's 2025 budget law.

Trump's agenda.t: Says Fitzpatrick talks like a moderate but sides with Trump when it counts.

pitch.t: Lower costs and "a return to fairness" for working families.

cands.name: Brian Fitzpatrick
cands.bio: Moderate Republican and former FBI agent.

Health care.t: Broke with GOP leaders to force a House vote on extending ACA subsidies.

Trump's agenda.t: Voted against the final version of the 2025 tax and spending law after backing the first House version.

pitch.t: Says hyper-partisanship has eroded trust in government.

cands.name: Marcy Kaptur
cands.bio: Democrat and the longest-serving woman in House history; beat Merrin by under 1 point in 2024.

Experience.t: Supporters say she keeps delivering for northwest Ohio from a senior Appropriations seat.

Abortion.t: Supports abortion rights and attacked Merrin's past support for strict limits.

pitch.t: Delivers for the region and its manufacturing base.

cands.name: Derek Merrin
cands.bio: Republican in a rematch of 2024; spoke at the RNC's midterm convention.

Experience.t: Says Kaptur has been in Congress longer than he's been alive and manufacturing declined on her watch.

Abortion.t: Supported strict abortion limits in the Ohio House, including criminal penalties, according to Kaptur's 2024 campaign.

pitch.t: An "America First" agenda: secure the border, cut taxes.

cands.name: Don Davis
cands.bio: Democrat, Air Force veteran and former state senator, running in a district redrawn to favor Republicans.

Abortion.t: Says Congress should codify Roe v. Wade.

Energy and climate.t: Voted to keep Biden-era clean energy tax credits.

cands.name: Laurie Buckhout
cands.bio: Republican backed by the NRCC's "MAGA Majority" program in a rematch she lost by about 6,000 votes.

Abortion.t: Personally pro-life; says states, not Washington, should decide.

Energy and climate.t: Says the U.S. can't solve climate change by regulating American companies out of business.

cands.name: Sam Forstag
cands.bio: Democrat endorsed by 14 unions; running for the open seat Rep. Ryan Zinke is leaving.

Cost of living.t: Focuses on housing, health care, child care and retirement security.

Money in politics.t: Says big money in politics is the thread connecting rising costs.

pitch.t: Congress needs more working people.

cands.name: Aaron Flint
cands.bio: Republican, former state director for Zinke and longtime National Guard and Reserve member.

Cost of living.t: No detailed plan found in campaign coverage.

Money in politics.t: Allies point to Forstag's past lobbying for the ACLU and Planned Parenthood.

pitch.t: "I am not guessing what people want; I have been listening to them for nearly two decades."

cands.name: Paige Cognetti
cands.bio: Former independent who joined the Democratic Party; won the primary unopposed.

Ethics.t: Centers her campaign on Bresnahan's stock trades and rooting out corruption.

Abortion.t: Says abortion "needs to be legal, it needs to be safe".

Energy and climate.t: Called the 2022 climate law a historic investment.

pitch.t: Transparency and accountability on Capitol Hill.

cands.name: Rob Bresnahan
cands.bio: First-term Republican in a district Trump carried by about 8 points.

Ethics.t: Has drawn scrutiny for stock trades despite campaigning on a congressional trading ban.

Abortion.t: Says he would never support a federal ban and that states should decide.

Energy and climate.t: Supported ending EPA power-plant emissions rules.

pitch.t: Says he will always stand with law enforcement.

cands.name: Rebecca Cooke
cands.bio: Democrat and daughter of dairy farmers; lost to Van Orden by about 11,000 votes in 2024. Endorsed by the Blue Dog PAC.

Health care.t: Targets drug companies for raising medicine prices.

Farms and rural economy.t: Vows to take on monopolies she says hollowed out family farms and rural economies.

pitch.t: Lower costs, fight corruption, back small businesses and agriculture.

cands.name: Derrick Van Orden
cands.bio: Republican and retired Navy SEAL seeking a third term.

Health care.t: Voted for the 2025 tax and spending law, which Cooke's allies say cut health care.

Farms and rural economy.t: No detailed position found in campaign coverage.

cands.name: Bobby Pulido
cands.bio: Democrat running as a centrist in a South Texas district Trump won by 18 points.

Cost of living.t: Focuses on gas prices, health care costs and De La Cruz's pro-Trump voting record.

Border and immigration.t: Lists immigration among his centrist priorities; calls the new district map unfair.

pitch.t: Says scrutiny of a former bandmate is a distraction from the issues.

cands.name: Monica De La Cruz
cands.bio: Republican who won reelection by 14 points in 2024.

Cost of living.t: Points to her record on the economy, Social Security and Medicare.

Border and immigration.t: Runs on border security and support for farmers.

pitch.t: Has attacked Pulido over his past association with a convicted sex offender.

cands.name: Katy Padilla Stout
cands.bio: Democrat and former San Antonio elementary teacher who now handles child welfare cases.

Guns.t: No detailed position found in campaign coverage.

Character.t: Runs a "common sense" pitch to conservative voters and says character still matters.

pitch.t: Highlights Herrera's past controversial remarks.

cands.name: Brandon Herrera
cands.bio: Republican known online as "The AK Guy," endorsed by the Freedom Caucus Fund; won the nomination after Rep. Tony Gonzales left the runoff.

Guns.t: First ran in 2024 against Gonzales's vote for the bipartisan gun safety law passed after Uvalde.

Character.t: Critics point to a history of edgy, controversial comments.

cands.name: Maura Healey
cands.bio: Democrat and former state attorney general seeking a second term; unopposed in the primary.

Taxes and costs.t: Points to a 2023 law with $1 billion in tax relief and says she has cut taxes; has proposed cutting the 24-cent state gas tax.

Housing.t: Says she is working to build homes as fast as possible to bring costs down.

Energy.t: Backs clean energy but says she won't stop natural gas work; asked the Trump administration on Oct. 1 to speed gas expansion into the state.

Trump.t: Ties Minogue to Trump and says tariffs, the war and federal cuts are raising costs in Massachusetts.

pitch.t: Says Trump's policies are making life more expensive and Minogue would go along with them.

cands.name: Mike Minogue
cands.bio: Republican, Army veteran and former Abiomed CEO; a self-funded first-time candidate.

Taxes and costs.t: Says overtaxation makes the state unaffordable and that Healey has fallen short despite record budgets.

Housing.t: Says any progress on housing came from Healey's Republican predecessor.

Energy.t: Wants more gas pipeline capacity and nuclear power, less reliance on wind and solar, and cuts to clean-energy fees he calls a "climate tax".

Trump.t: Calls himself a longtime independent who would work with any president.

pitch.t: Says Healey is "bankrupting our state" and has no plan for the exploding budget.
